title: Features
summary: What changes from Classic, and what every Nightcap player should know.
body:
Plan equipment for your classes

The loot finder matches equipment usable by any held class, with an optional all-selected-classes mode, active-era filtering and source mobs, locations and calculated drop chances. Production content refreshes automatically every fifteen minutes. This tool does not change loot or equipment rules.

Live testing — Hate Keeper in Commonlands: Find the Plane of Hate Keeper in East Commonlands at /loc -1570,-346,3, between Mirielle and Khalure in the travel area. Raid, Grind and return entry lead to Hate; private Hate instances retain an entrance Keeper. Public and private Hate entry require level 46; GM status is no longer required. The server update is installed. The owner confirmed the relocation, Commonlands visibility and Hate travel. Broader dungeon balance and full-clear QA remain separate.

Try the experimental Build Lab to compare stat changes and test spell priorities against explicit combat assumptions. Full gear, AA and pet effects are not automatically modeled.

Live testing: The Classic raid rewards give every dungeon three exclusive designs. The 14 added dungeons contribute 42 designs in two qualities; all 414 dungeon rewards are MAGIC. Fear, Hate and Sky receive lore-driven relics and equipped utility clicks. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

Live testing: Every Classic dungeon coverage adds the same Raid/Grind choices in 21 combat dungeon zones, including Fear, Hate and Sky. All 21 are installed for live testing; gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

Quest ingredient qualities - live testing

Better ordinary qualities can satisfy Normal quest ingredients, including the Aviak Charm for Crafted Gauntlets. The quest keeps its configured reward. See ingredient rules and limits.

Live testing: Five reviewed class-armor families now give guaranteed Ascended rewards. Substantial repeatable quests qualify; cheap/basic hand-ins remain excluded.

Live testing: Game update 2026102204 repairs the native waist binding in the robe bodies added for seven Classic races. Item power and held-class equipment access are unchanged. Native visual acceptance remains open. Robe update.

Level-scaled AA — live testing: Earn two AA per level while leveling. From level 1, use the AA +/− buttons to choose 0–100%; 100% pauses leveling so you can grind AA where you prefer. Close EverQuest and update through launcher Play for game 2026102301. Existing points, purchases and partial progress stay intact. AA progression and examples.

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

Live AA testing: All 16 classes have more earned AA options: 75 newly available lines, 111 expanded lines and Druid access to Healing Boon. The latest custom behavior update retires Spell Casting Subtlety and obsolete Silent Casting modifiers, with recorded-cost refunds. Classic remains level 50. Reconnect and turn Recommended AA off to browse your held classes. Read the AA update.

Live testing: The combined item, spell, pet equipment and melee release is installed for live testing. It preserves Classic level 50 and earned progression. See the updated combat, equipment and pet guides below.

Ordinary eligible equipment and bags have a 20% Polished, 5% Exalted and 1% Ascended chance per drop. Read the loot quality rules.

The major departures from Classic, with the rules you need before your next adventure. Start with a topic below, then follow its guide for requirements and limits.

These systems are deployed for live testing. Balance and some gameplay checks remain ongoing. In development lists work that is not yet available.

Build one character from three classes

Three classes from level 1

Keep your starting class and choose two different extra classes. Your held classes shape spell access, equipment, skills, and base health and mana.

Choose your classes →

AA progression from the beginning

Allowed AA ranks open at level 1. With AA allocation at 0%, earn full leveling XP plus two AA per level. The AA +/− controls work from level 1; choose 100% to pause leveling and focus on AA. Points and prerequisites still matter.

Understand AA progression →

Scribe spells ahead of time

Eligible scrolls can enter your spellbook early. Memorizing and casting still require the normal level for a class you hold.

Learn the spell rules →

A roster of companions

Multiple summoned pets, selected-pet or All-pets commands, and stored pet armor support a multiclass roster.

Manage your pets →

Earn, trade and upgrade your gear

Stronger item qualities and zone rewards

Ordinary tiered gear and the 48-zone reward hunt offer distinct quality families. Hunt augments fit six armor locations and add heroic stats.

Explore rewards and sockets →

Turn duplicates into upgrades

Use three Base zone rewards for Polished, then four matching copies for each higher step. Veyra’s reusable box also upgrades eligible ordinary Polished and Exalted items. The box also accepts three identical eligible Normal/Base copies for Polished.

See the upgrade recipes →

Free trading and no LORE limit

Trade formerly restricted and attuned items and keep duplicate LORE items. Inventory space, temporary lifetime and other item rules still apply.

Read trading and resale rules →

Equipment for your held classes

Wear ordinary equipment allowed by any held class, regardless of playable race. Other restrictions, including slot, level and deity, remain.

Check equipment eligibility →

Prepare in the tunnel, then explore

Raid or Grind in all 21 Classic dungeons

Choose normal respawning enemies or harder enemies with permanent deaths. Earn personal boss-checklist rewards; Raid final bosses add exclusive loot.

Choose your dungeon mode →

A shared home base

New characters start with a kit and 100 platinum in the East Commonlands tunnel. Trainers, spell shops, supplies, banking, buffs and travel services are gathered there.

Meet the tunnel services →

Travel, discovery and private dungeons

Use tunnel travel services, discover waypoint destinations and enter supported personal dungeon instances. Ancient Attunement recalls you home without changing your bind.

Plan your journey →

Lasting blessings; temporary combat abilities

Ordinary beneficial blessings persist on players and owned pets. Temporary AA effects, disciplines and short-duration effects retain their timers.

Know which effects last →

Keep fighting while you cast

Damage-over-time spells cast instantly, and melee autoattacks can continue during casting. Mana costs, reuse, resistance and control effects still matter.

Read the combat changes →

Less upkeep between adventures

Food and drink are optional. Normal death retains EXP, level, AA progress, carried equipment, inventory, money and memorized spell gems; beneficial buffs are lost. Preparation, earned gear and encounter execution still matter.

Read combat and recovery →

Healing without changing your target

Ordinary heals can heal your own permanent pet. With an enemy selected, eligible heals still redirect to you. Specialized spells retain their target rules.

Check healing targets →

Spend more time playing

Stacked materials and Craft All

Stackable items support at least 100, preserving larger limits. Use stacks without manually splitting every ingredient. Repeat a recipe with Craft All while retaining normal recipe requirements, success chances and skill gains.

Use the crafting controls →

Advanced loot and bulk selling

Use personal loot queues, loot preferences and group rolls. Sell All keeps bags and casting supplies; bank valuable gear before selling.

Learn the loot interface →

One launcher, current updates

The normal Nightcap shortcut delivers managed game/interface updates and dated patch summaries. Keep your existing folder and personal settings.

Update before playing →

Keep up with changes

Read Recent changes for dated updates. Each release review covers affected guides, commands, item and zone pages, and this Features overview together.

Live testing: Raid and Grind dungeon modes are available from all 21 dungeon Keepers. Existing legacy runs keep their original behavior until expiry or reset. Gameplay and balance acceptance remain open.

More guidance and independent attacks

The optional Recommended AA filter helps you choose early survival and damage upgrades. Six basic Monk attacks have separate cooldowns, and cooldown duration repairs prevent several excessive lockouts. Activated AA families now keep separate cooldowns, including Rampage and Purify Body. Gameplay and balance checks continue.

Item and spell progression

Reviewed Ascended items, modest starter upgrades and stronger dungeon budgets bring item progression closer to the observed THJ references. Additive Spell Damage and direct heroic-stat bonuses, paged pet equipment and earned shield/melee synergies are installed together. Player combat and balance checks remain open.

The Vigil of the Dawn — live testing

Camil’s level-50 Paladin story in Chapterhouse uses native Tasks, persistent personal chapters and a one-time helmet claim. Custom enemies and encounter mechanics support a demanding capstone, with era-curated rewards. Read the quest guide and reward catalog.
